research_topic: Cell Federation, Sync Engines, CRDTs, and Envelope-Based Distributed Architecture for Tribunus
transcript_summary: Research was conducted to deepen the evidence base for ADR 0014 (Tribunus Cell Federation), which defines Cells as sovereign local authority domains that exchange signed envelopes rather than syncing databases. The research investigated ElectricSQL/PowerSync sync engines, CRDT libraries (Automerge v2, Yjs), hub-and-spoke vs P2P sync tradeoffs, envelope-based federation patterns, local-first software principles (Kleppmann, Ink & Switch), and DID-based cell identity for cross-domain authorization.

research_findings.title: ElectricSQL — Shape-Based Sync to Agent Platform Evolution
research_findings.finding: ElectricSQL rebranded to Electric (electric.ax) — positioning as 'the agent platform built on sync.' Released 1.0 March 2025. Uses Shape-Based Sync consuming PostgreSQL logical replication stream. Shapes define data subsets analogous to live queries. Supports 1M+ concurrent readers with 99% CDN cache hit rate. Expanded into Electric Agents (long-lived logical agents), Durable Streams, PGlite integration. Blog posts on AI agents as CRDT peers (April 2026). CRDT-based conflict resolution. Primarily a read-path engine — writes expected to be handled by application's existing backend API.

research_findings.title: PowerSync — Bucket-Based Sync with Broader DB Support
research_findings.finding: PowerSync uses explicit 'sync buckets' — partitions of data organizing rows synced to users' devices. Sync Streams defined via SQL-like queries. Backend-agnostic: PostgreSQL, MongoDB (GA March 2025), MySQL, SQL Server (alpha Dec 2025). Wider backend compatibility than ElectricSQL (PostgreSQL only). Local writes to SQLite queued for upload to developer's backend API. Default 'last write wins' conflict resolution, customizable. Strong built-in tooling for offline writes.

research_findings.title: Automerge v2 vs Yjs — CRDT Tradeoffs
research_findings.finding: Automerge 2.0 (Jan 2023) — ground-up Rust rewrite with JS (WASM) and C bindings. JSON-like data model. Full history retention enables time travel, undo/redo, audit trails. Automerge Repo 2.0 (May 2025) — 'batteries-included' toolkit for local-first apps. Automerge 3.0 under development through 2026. Positioning: 'PostgreSQL for local-first applications.' Yjs — built around composable data structures. Does NOT retain full history by default. Typically faster and produces smaller updates for large text documents (benchmarks late 2025). Available in JS and Rust. Eg-walker (Gentle & Kleppmann, EuroSys 2025, Best Artifact Award) blurs OT/CRDT boundary — CRDT-compatible decentralization with OT-like performance, order-of-magnitude less memory.

research_findings.title: Hub-and-Spoke vs Peer-to-Peer Sync Tradeoffs
research_findings.finding: Hub-and-spoke: central hub as authoritative data repository, spokes store local copies, sync through hub. Advantages: centralized control/management, simpler consistency and conflict resolution, straightforward scaling, easier security/permissions. Disadvantages: single point of failure, latency/bandwidth dependency, hub infrastructure costs. Peer-to-peer: devices exchange data directly without persistent central server. Advantages: resilience, faster local sync, improved privacy, reduced server load, works in disconnected environments. Disadvantages: complex consistency (requires CRDTs), discovery/connectivity overhead, complex security, scaling challenges. Hybrid models common: hub acts as relay/bridge for P2P-capable clients — handles peer discovery, NAT traversal, offline message queuing, partial replication. Cell federation can layer both approaches.

research_findings.title: Envelope-Based Federation vs Row Sync
research_findings.finding: Signed envelopes: secure container encapsulating data payload, digital signature, metadata (timestamp, source, schema version), digital certificate. Ensures authenticity and integrity. Maps to ActivityPub-style or JWS-based federation patterns. Receipt-based exchange: sender receives acknowledgment of successful receipt/processing — guarantees delivery, enables idempotency in distributed transactions. Event-Carried State Transfer (ECST) reduces consumer fetch calls. Row sync (ElectricSQL/PowerSync approach): exact row-level replication, each row is a unit of sync, changes detected via logical replication or change tracking. Envelope approach adds semantic event metadata enabling richer federation — events have meaning beyond raw row changes. Row sync simpler for DB-to-DB; envelope sync better for heterogeneous systems and cross-cell federation where cells may have different internal representations.

research_findings.title: Local-First Patterns — 2026 State
research_findings.finding: Ink & Switch local-first manifesto (2019): seven ideals — fast local interaction, multi-device sync, offline operation, real-time collaboration, long-term preservation, security/privacy, user ownership. CRDTs as 'foundational technology.' OT vs CRDT (2026 mature position): OT better for centralized server-mediated collaboration (Google Docs) — lower overhead, proven at scale, complex transformation rules, offline branches hard. CRDTs better for offline-first, P2P, multi-device, user-owned data — no central sequencer, robust under partitions, metadata overhead, memory cost. Kleppmann's QCon London March 2026 keynote: 'Mitigating Geopolitical Risks with Local-First Software and atproto' — local-first as technological sovereignty. Local-first not suited for domains requiring single authoritative state (financial ledgers, inventory of scarce goods).

research_findings.title: Git-Based Collaboration Models for Cell Data Distribution
research_findings.finding: Git provides patterns applicable to cell federation: sparse checkout (selectively populate working directory with specific directories/files, cone mode for fast pattern matching), shallow clone (--depth=N limits commit history depth), partial clone (--filter downloads only needed object data, reported average clone time reduction 88.6%, >99% for largest repos), blobless clone (--filter=blob:none downloads all commits/trees but defers blob download). Recommended combined strategy: partial clone (blobless) + sparse checkout. Microsoft's Scalar and VFS for Git use these under the hood. Git 2.52 (late 2025): introspection + tree-level blame improvements. Git's DAG model maps to CRDT version vectors — potential for git-like data replication between cells.

research_findings.title: DID-Based Cell Identity for Federation
research_findings.finding: DID standardization (2026): W3C DIDs v1.1 candidate recommendation. eIDAS 2.0 regulation (effective Jan 2026) drove adoption. 45M+ active DIDs across chains, monthly growth >15%. Google and Apple integrated W3C-compliant DID methods into identity frameworks. DIDs as interoperability bridge connecting centralized, federated, and decentralized identity. VCs enable cross-domain auth without shared identity stores. Capability-based security: VCs function as explicit capabilities, not broad identity grants. Zero-knowledge proofs enable selective disclosure. DID-based cell identity implications: each cell gets a DID as its stable identifier, cell capabilities encoded as Verifiable Credentials, DID documents contain service endpoints for cell sync relays, key rotation without identifier change, no central PKI needed. Cross-cell authorization through signed capability grants.

implementation_specs.title: Tribunus Cell Federation Protocol
implementation_specs.description: Design and implement the envelope-based federation protocol for Tribunus Cells — including envelope format, signing, validation, delivery, retry, and import semantics. Cells exchange signed content-light envelopes rather than syncing databases. No Cell has remote write authority over another Cell's PGlite store.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format defined with type, version, timestamp, source DID, target DID, payload hash, signature, correlation ID, and TTL
Envelope signing uses DID-based keys with Ed25519 signatures
Receiving Cell validates signature, schema version, TTL, and source authorization
Delivery receipts guarantee at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing
Federation worker in Valkey manages outgoing queues, retries, and heartbeat with lease-based lifecycle
Each Cell maintains an imported-external-event table in PGlite for recording validated envelopes
Cross-cell authorization uses signed capability grants (capped delegation with expiry)
